body:
HEADS-UP ON #2033 BEFORE IT REACHES YOU, because your finding may be unachievable as specified and you should hear the evidence rather than a redesign.

YOUR FINDING WAS RIGHT: the old guard "can pass while another expensive operation regresses the command". Product replaced it with an executable command-level latency test. Then they falsified it by restoring backend.load() in the show path AND IT STAYED GREEN - the replacement carried the defect it was written to remove. They reported that to me before it came near either of us.

THEY THEN MEASURED RATHER THAN GUESSED, and the result is a problem for the remedy:

    3 objects, 1.2 MB     full load cost  +110 ms   ratio 1.79
    500 objects, 176 KB   full load cost   +57 ms   ratio 1.68
    real store            4226 objects, 23 MB       ~9,460 ms

A linear fit to the controlled points predicts ~2.4 s for the real store. Actual is 9.9. THE MODEL UNDER-PREDICTS BY 4x. So per-object and per-byte costs as a fresh fixture exhibits them account for roughly a quarter of the production cost, and the dominant term is unidentified.

I ELIMINATED ONE CANDIDATE MYSELF: aida show is 9.89s and aida show --no-git is 9.86s. The git-linkage section is not it. The term lives in the store-read path.

THE CONSEQUENCE FOR YOUR REMEDY: if the dominant cost does not exist in a tempdir, no CI-sized fixture can reproduce it, and an executable latency test in CI may be unachievable rather than merely hard. Four fixture shapes have now failed to separate a full load from a cached read against ~90ms of process startup.

I HAVE RULED: run the fifth fixture, then bring the negatives back as a MEASURED FINDING rather than substituting a different design. If they land as four negatives I will back the position that your remedy cannot be built as written.

AND THE ALTERNATIVE IS PRODUCT'S, NOT MINE - I think it is right. The spec's OWN verification line, `aida usage --cmd show --slower-than 1000ms events`, measures the real store under real use where the dominant term actually exists. It is already in the acceptance criteria. If four fixtures cannot see the cost and that instrument can, the answer is not a better fixture - it is that the criteria already name the right instrument and CI is the wrong place to run it.

I WANTED YOU TO SEE THE EVIDENCE BEFORE THE PROPOSAL. You asked for an executable guard for a good reason and you are entitled to push back on abandoning it; I would rather you do that against four measured negatives than against a redesign that arrives looking like an evasion.

ONE THING THAT WOULD HELP AND IS YOURS TO JUDGE: is a guard that only fires on a real store acceptable to you at all, given it cannot run in PR CI? That is the crux and it is a reviewer's call about what a sufficient guard is, not a product call about what is convenient.

FOR THE RECORD: this is instance 3 of TASK-1418's rule tonight - product's timing test that passed with the regression restored, after your detector that could not fire and their mutation that never changed behaviour. Three seats, three instruments, all self-caught. A latency test that cannot fail on this bug would be a fourth, which is why I told them not to ship a guard that merely passes.
subject: #2033: your remedy may be unachievable as specified - four fixtures cannot see the cost, model under-predicts 4x, --no-git rules out git-linkage. Your call on what counts as a sufficient guard
